findings.claim: ADR-0014 designs the intake as a web issue form only. Coding agents file issues with `gh issue create --body/--body-file` or REST POST /issues, and issue forms (required fields, dropdowns, checkboxes) do not apply on those paths. So every field ADR-0014 makes 'required' is unenforced for the reporter the owner targets.
findings.evidence: `gh issue create --help` (gh 2.39.1): '-T, --template name    Template name to use as starting body text'; '-F, --body-file file'. GitHub docs (syntax-for-issue-forms, configuring-issue-templates) describe validations only for the web form; cli/cli#5865 'Support for issue forms' is open. gemini-cli/.gemini/skills/github-issue-creator/SKILL.md:39-47: its agent writes the body to a temp file and runs `gh issue create --title ... --body-file <temp_file_path>`. ADR-0014:57 lists only form widgets (dropdown, textarea, checkboxes).
findings.fix: Add to ADR-0014: (a) a machine-readable agent file `.github/AGENT_ISSUE.md` that defines the body as fixed `### ` headings (the same headings the web form emits, so both paths parse alike); (b) a CI intake check (finding 2). Proposed files are in this JSON under `files`.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 2f3a2c2a/a0781c53 2026-03-02 'Add GitHub issue/PR templates and contributing guide'; hardened by e3ea9ad3 2026-03-24 'strengthen bug report template — require repro, error output, self-debug'. ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'Full error output now REQUIRED', 'Pre-submission checklist with mandatory checkboxes'. REGRESSION_RISK: those 'required' marks never bound gh/API filers; v2 copies the same blind spot. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: keep the required data, enforce it after creation in CI, not in the form.

findings.claim: No workflow validates issue bodies. ADR-0014 relies on the report digest but nothing recomputes it, and v1 has no `issues:` workflow either. Invalid or v1 bodies reach the maintainer unchecked.
findings.evidence: tickets/round4-evidence.json templates-debug F2: "'grep -ln issues: .github/workflows/*' gives rc=1 (no match)". ADR-0014 §5 table (lines 55-61) has no workflow row; ADR-0014:77 'the digest verifies' is only a GP11 unit assertion.
findings.fix: Add `.github/workflows/issue-intake.yml` (on issues opened/edited/reopened) running `.github/scripts/issue-intake.mjs`: split the body by `### ` headings, find lines `ctx-report: 1`..`digest:`, check required rows, recompute sha256, then label `has-report|no-report` or label `needs-report`, comment the missing items with the fix command, close as not planned, and reopen on a passing edit. No regex (owner rule). Tested in scratchpad: valid body -> ok; one changed row -> 'digest does not match'.

findings.claim: `issues` workflows and issue templates take effect only from the default branch, but ADR-0011 keeps `main` frozen on v1 and ADR-0014 does not say on which branch its files land. Put on `v2`, the form, config.yml and the intake check never run.
findings.evidence: GitHub Actions docs, events-that-trigger-workflows/issues: 'This event will only trigger a workflow run if the workflow file exists on the default branch.' Configuring issue templates: 'Commit your file to the default branch of your repository.' ADR-0011:11 '`main` | v1, frozen'. ADR-0013:3 'workflows may go to `main`'.
findings.fix: State in ADR-0014 that `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*`, `.github/AGENT_ISSUE.md`, `.github/scripts/issue-intake*.mjs` and `.github/workflows/issue-intake.yml` go to `main` (allowed by ADR-0013:3; `package.json` untouched, so ADR-0011:15 still holds), in the same owner-approved step that turns Issues on (ADR-0014:67).

findings.claim: The digest is not defined well enough to recompute: ADR-0014 does not say which bytes it covers (which lines, LF vs CRLF, final newline, fence). The web form returns CRLF and a fenced block; without a byte rule the CI check gives false 'edited' results. Also an unkeyed sha256 proves only 'not changed by accident', not authenticity; the ADR should say so.
findings.evidence: ADR-0014:25 'It starts with `ctx-report: 1` and ends with `digest: <sha256>`' (no byte rule). ADR-0014:77 'the digest verifies' with no algorithm input defined.
findings.fix: Define: digest = sha256 hex (64 lowercase) of every report line from `ctx-report: 1` up to the line before `digest:`, each line ending in LF, UTF-8, no fence. The checker strips CR and fence lines before it hashes. Add GP11 cases: CRLF body, fenced body, one byte changed.

findings.claim: The report holds only 7-day aggregates. The owner wants maximum debug data, and the earlier design had a typed decision journal for the issue form (last hook decisions, deny rows). ADR-0014 dropped it, and the only reader for it was a CLI that G12-G14 removed, so the 'last decisions', 'hook journal rows' and 'deny journal rows' have no safe path into an issue.
findings.evidence: tickets/round4-evidence.json line 670 design §6 'DEBUG JOURNAL (feeds the v2 issue form) One row per decision: {ts, agent, agentVersion, transport, session8, agentType, tool, sig, astShape (node types only), parse{ok, code, ms}, pred, src, n, p90, budget, decision, repeat, decideMs}. 'context-mode debug --last 20' prints the rows'. PRD-v2.md:196 G12-G14 'no CLI'. ADR-0014:28-36 rows: only counts (`deny_7d`, hook error codes top 5).
findings.fix: Add a `report:"issue"` input to ctx_doctor that appends up to 20 typed `decision:` rows (tool enum, astShape node types, parse code enum, pred/budget ints, decision enum, ms) and up to 10 `hook_error:` rows (code enum, hook enum, day), all through the same typed scanner (ADR-0014 §3), still within 4,096 B. The agent never reads context.db itself. Re-measure the worst case for GP11.

findings.claim: Redaction covers only the report block. The free-text fields (what happened, steps that must 'name the denied tool and the alternative') make the agent paste real commands, URLs, paths and the user's prompt into a public issue. That is the #1141 leak class again, through the text fields.
findings.evidence: ADR-0014:57 'steps must name the denied tool and the alternative it gave'. The ADR-0008 deny message carries `"code":<original command>` (ADR-0008 Deny message block). isall.json #1141 '[Bug]: ctx-debug.sh dumps plaintext secrets from settings.json — bug_report.yml requires pasting this into public issues'. v1 bug_report.yml:91-103 'Exact prompt that triggered the bug (REQUIRED)... the literal prompt text'.
findings.fix: In AGENT_ISSUE.md list what the agent must not send (configs, .env, MCP lists, logs, transcripts, file bodies, tool output, user prompts as typed, paths, names, hosts, tokens, env values, screenshots). Ask for a repro in GP style: setup in an empty dir with sizes not content, a short prompt the agent writes, the tool call with `<placeholders>`. Require a 'the user read this body' check before `gh issue create`.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY e3ea9ad3 2026-03-24 'chore: strengthen bug report template — require repro, error output, self-debug' (exact-prompt field: git log -S'Exact prompt that triggered'). ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'Without this, we cannot reproduce.' REGRESSION_RISK: dropping the prompt loses repro power. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: keep a required prompt, but one the agent writes for an empty dir, plus 'Reproduced: yes|no'. ctx-debug.sh: 4eba5aaf 2026-04-03 'add cross-platform debug script' intent 'config files for all 12 adapters with redaction'; #1141 shows that redaction failed, so v2 must not ask for config files at all.

findings.claim: ADR-0014 says the report is a fixed `key: value` block with a digest; TECH-SPEC §3.9 and the skill draft say ctx_doctor returns a Markdown table that the skill shows 'unchanged'. A table cannot be the digest-checked block, and a model that re-renders a table breaks the digest.
findings.evidence: TECH-SPEC.md:211 '`ctx_stats`, `ctx_doctor`, `ctx_upgrade` return Markdown tables'. docs/v2/prompt/drafts.md:79 'Call the ctx_doctor tool and show its table to the user unchanged.' ADR-0014:24-25 'a fixed list of `key: value` lines ... starts with `ctx-report: 1`'.
findings.fix: Specify both outputs: the table for people, then one fenced ```ctx-report block. The tool description and the skill text say to copy the block byte for byte for an issue. The intake check accepts fenced or bare blocks.

findings.claim: The planned bug.yml is written for humans ('Run /ctx-doctor, or tell the agent ...'), but the owner rule says the template is for AI agents. Agents read `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.yml` as their spec (gemini-cli's issue skill does), so the template text must be agent instructions in ADR-0005 style (no caps imperatives, reasons given).
findings.evidence: ADR-0014:57 'Run `/ctx-doctor`, or tell the agent: call the ctx_doctor tool.' gemini-cli/.gemini/skills/github-issue-creator/SKILL.md:21-35 'Locate Template... Read the content of the identified template file... prepare values for each `id`'. v1 bug_report.yml:13 '### PRs > Issues. Always.' and :85 '**Issues without debug output will be closed immediately.**' (caps/threat tone ADR-0005 rejects).
findings.fix: Rewrite bug.yml and config.yml to point agents at `.github/AGENT_ISSUE.md` first (config.yml contact link 'Coding agents start here'; CONTRIBUTING.md; ctx_doctor FAIL text ends with the AGENT_ISSUE URL). Run `docs/v2/prompt/lint.mjs files .github/AGENT_ISSUE.md .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.yml` in CI.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 69bfd0f4 2026-03-05 'Add contribution manifesto to issue templates' and e3ea9ad3 'Stronger language: PRs preferred'. ORIGINAL_INTENT: push reporters to self-debug and send PRs. REGRESSION_RISK: none for v2; PRs are closed (ADR-0014). SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: keep the 'debug first' intent as 'call ctx_doctor', drop the PR push.

findings.claim: ADR-0014 keeps CONTRIBUTING.md ('issues only, with the doctor report'); the round-5 README design deletes it ('One path: the README Support section'). README design also says 'Issues ... are closed', which conflicts with ADR-0014 owner step 1 'Turn Issues back on'.
findings.evidence: ADR-0014:61. tickets/round5-evidence.json:126 'CONTRIBUTING.md: delete. One path: the README Support section states the policy.' and '12. Support (5). "Issues, discussions and outside pull requests are closed."'. ADR-0014:67.
findings.fix: Keep CONTRIBUTING.md as a 10-line pointer to AGENT_ISSUE.md (GitHub links it from the new-issue page, agents look for it), and fix the README Support line to 'Issues: filed by your agent, see .github/AGENT_ISSUE.md; no pull requests'.

findings.claim: docs/v2/README.md says there is no doctor; the whole v2 issue intake depends on ctx_doctor (ADR-0010, ADR-0014, PRD-v2.md:289 9 tools).
findings.evidence: docs/v2/README.md:101 '7 tools: ...'; :103 'No doctor, upgrade or uninstall commands.' PRD-v2.md:289 '9 tools — ... ctx_doctor, ctx_upgrade, ctx_purge'.
findings.fix: Update docs/v2/README.md §9 to 9 tools and the 3 skills, as decided in PRD §(late) and ADR-0010.

findings.claim: Owner step 'Create the labels' names no labels, and labels that do not exist are not added by forms. The intake flow needs a fixed set.
findings.evidence: ADR-0014:68 '2. Create the labels.' round4-evidence F9 'A label that does not exist is not added'.
findings.fix: List them: bug, has-report, no-report, needs-report, v1-frozen. The workflow skips issues labeled v1-frozen.

findings.claim: GP11 tests the report but not the intake check. A parser change could reject every valid issue and nobody would see it before users do.
findings.evidence: ADR-0014:71-79 test list: secrets, has_space, size, digest only.
findings.fix: Add a keyless golden test: the GP11 report pasted via (a) the web-form body (CRLF, ```ctx-report fence, `_No response_`), (b) a `--body-file` body, (c) one edited row, (d) a 'no:' status -> expected JSON from issue-intake.mjs. Run under node:test in CI on v2.

files..github/AGENT_ISSUE.md:
# Filing a context-mode issue (for coding agents)

You are a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Pi, OpenCode, Copilot) and your user asked you to report a context-mode problem. This file tells you what to collect, how to collect it, what to leave out, and the exact body to send. A GitHub Action reads every new issue and checks it against this format, so a body that follows it gets triaged and one that does not gets a comment that lists what is missing.

Why it is strict: one person maintains context-mode for 10 agents on 3 operating systems. A fix starts from the doctor report and a repro that runs in a fresh directory. Free text without them cannot be acted on.

## 1. Before you write anything

1. Search for the same problem: `gh issue list -R mksglu/context-mode --state all --search "<error code or check id>"`. If an open issue matches, add a comment with your ctx-report block to that issue instead of opening a new one.
2. Only v2 gets fixes. If the ctx_doctor tool does not exist in this agent, or its output does not start with `ctx-report: 1`, the user runs v1. Tell the user to install v2 (https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode#install) and stop; v1 issues are closed as `v1-frozen`.
3. Work in the agent and the project where the problem happens. If the user asks you to report a problem in a different agent, ask the user to run `/ctx-doctor` there and give you the block.

## 2. What to collect, and how

| Item | How you get it | Where it goes |
|---|---|---|
| ctx-report block | Call the `ctx_doctor` tool with `{"report":"issue"}`. Copy its fenced block unchanged, from `ctx-report: 1` to the `digest:` line. On Claude Code the user can also run `/ctx-doctor`. | section `Report` |
| why there is no report | If ctx_doctor cannot run, pick one reason from the list in section `Report status` | section `Report status` |
| Node version | `node --version` | section `Node` |
| filing agent | your own name, version and model id, for example `claude-code 2.1.283 claude-opus-5-5`. Use your CLI's `--version` output. | section `Filed by` |
| context-mode error line | the one line the tool result showed, starting with its code, for example `E_DB_BUSY`. Send the code and the fixed text that follows it; leave out any path or command that appears after it. | section `What happened` |
| repro | see section 4 | section `Steps to reproduce` |

The ctx-report block already holds the data the maintainer needs and nothing private: version and commit, agent and agent version (from MCP clientInfo), install mode, OS, Node and node:sqlite and FTS5, MCP protocol versions, enforcement mode, config differences as counts, v1 leftovers, project source and path facts (`has_space`, `non_ascii`, `max_len`), database integrity, index counts, hook round trips, hook error codes over 7 days, the deny summary, checks D1 to D10, and in issue mode the last 20 hook decisions and the last 10 hook errors as typed rows. Every value in it passed a typed scanner, so you do not need to clean it, and an edited block fails the digest check.

Get this data only through ctx_doctor. Reading `context.db`, the hook journal or the host config yourself puts paths, commands and file text into your context and into a public issue, and it is the leak that v1 issue #1141 reported.

## 3. What you leave out

These can hold secrets or private code, and the issue is public:

- settings files, `.env` files, MCP config files, `claude mcp list` or `codex mcp list` output
- agent debug logs, transcripts, session files, stack traces
- file contents, command output, `ctx_search` or `ctx_execute` results
- the user's prompts as typed; write a minimal prompt of your own instead (section 4)
- absolute paths, user names, host names, repo names of the user's project, IP addresses, emails
- tokens, keys, cookies, environment variable values
- screenshots

If a detail seems needed and it is on this list, describe it in one sentence with placeholders (`<home>`, `<project>`, `<token>`) and ask the user before you send it.

## 4. Steps to reproduce

Write steps that a maintainer's agent can run in a new empty directory, in the same style as the project's golden tests:

1. Setup: the commands that create the directory and files, with sizes instead of content (for example `head -c 300000 /dev/urandom | base64 > big.txt`).
2. Agent and mode: which agent, which install mode (from the report).
3. The prompt: one short prompt you wrote that triggers the problem in that directory.
4. The tool call: tool name and the input shape, with values replaced by placeholders, for example `Bash {"command":"curl -s <url>"}`.
5. Observed: what context-mode did (deny, rewrite, allow, hint, error code) and, for a deny, which alternative it named and what happened when the agent used it.
6. Expected: what should have happened instead.

Run the steps once yourself in a temporary directory before you send them if the user agrees; say in the body whether you did (`Reproduced: yes|no`).

## 5. The body

Create the issue with a body file, because multi-line Markdown breaks in shell quoting:

```
gh issue create -R mksglu/context-mode --title "<check id or error code>: <short summary>" --label bug --body-file <file>
```

Use these headings, in this order, with this exact text. The web form produces the same headings, so both paths are checked the same way.

````
### Report status

yes

### Report

```ctx-report
ctx-report: 1
...
digest: <64 hex>
```

### Node

v24.11.0

### Filed by

claude-code 2.1.283 claude-opus-5-5

### What happened

E_DB_BUSY context.db is locked by another writer

### Expected

The search returns results.

### Steps to reproduce

Reproduced: yes
1. ...

### Checks

- [x] The report comes from ctx_doctor in the agent and project where the problem happens, or Report status names why not.
- [x] I searched existing issues for the same code.
- [x] The body holds none of the items in "What you leave out".
- [x] The user read this body before I sent it.
````

`Report status` is `yes`, or one of these lines, and then `Report` holds `_No response_`:

- `no: ctx_doctor is not in the tool list`
- `no: the context-mode MCP server is failed or not connected`
- `no: ctx_doctor returned an error` (put its one error line in `What happened`)

Show the user the full body and the title before you run `gh issue create`, and send it only after the user agrees. The user owns the GitHub account the issue comes from.

## 6. After you send it

The intake check comments within a minute. If it lists missing items, fix the body with `gh issue edit <n> -R mksglu/context-mode --body-file <file>`; the check runs again on every edit and reopens the issue when the body passes. Pull requests are closed on this repo, so do not offer a patch; put your analysis of the cause, if you have one, as a short paragraph under `What happened`.

name: Bug report (v2)
description: For coding agents filing for their user. Read .github/AGENT_ISSUE.md first; this form makes the same body.
title: "<check id or error code>: <summary>"
labels: ["bug"]
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: |
        Coding agent: read https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/blob/main/.github/AGENT_ISSUE.md and create the issue with `gh issue create --body-file`. A workflow checks every body against that file, from the web form and from the API alike.
        Get the report by calling the ctx_doctor tool with {"report":"issue"} in the agent and project where the problem happens. Paste the block unchanged; an edited block fails the digest check.
        Do not send settings, .env or MCP config files, logs, transcripts, file contents, paths, tokens or the user's own prompts.
  - type: dropdown
    id: report-status
    attributes:
      label: Report status
      options:
        - "yes"
        - "no: ctx_doctor is not in the tool list"
        - "no: the context-mode MCP server is failed or not connected"
        - "no: ctx_doctor returned an error"
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: report
    attributes:
      label: Report
      description: The block from `ctx-report: 1` to `digest:`. Empty only when Report status is a "no" line.
      render: ctx-report
  - type: input
    id: node
    attributes:
      label: Node
      description: Output of `node --version`
      placeholder: v24.11.0
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: input
    id: filed-by
    attributes:
      label: Filed by
      description: Agent name, agent version, model id
      placeholder: claude-code 2.1.283 claude-opus-5-5
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: what-happened
    attributes:
      label: What happened
      description: The context-mode error code and its fixed text, without paths or commands. Then your cause analysis, if any, in one short paragraph.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: expected
    attributes:
      label: Expected
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: steps
    attributes:
      label: Steps to reproduce
      description: "First line: Reproduced: yes|no. Then setup in an empty directory, agent and install mode, a short prompt you wrote, the tool call with placeholders, observed, expected."
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: checkboxes
    id: checks
    attributes:
      label: Checks
      options:
        - label: The report comes from ctx_doctor in the agent and project where the problem happens, or Report status names why not.
          required: true
        - label: I searched existing issues for the same code.
          required: true
        - label: The body holds none of the items in "What you leave out".
          required: true
        - label: The user read this body before I sent it.
          required: true

files..github/workflows/issue-intake.yml:
# Must live on the DEFAULT branch: GitHub runs `issues` workflows only from there.
name: issue-intake
on:
  issues:
    types: [opened, edited, reopened]
permissions:
  issues: write
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: issue-intake-${{ github.event.issue.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  check:
    if: ${{ !github.event.issue.pull_request && !contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'v1-frozen') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          sparse-checkout: .github
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Check body
        id: check
        env:
          BODY: ${{ github.event.issue.body }}
        run: |
          printf '%s' "$BODY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/body.md"
          node .github/scripts/issue-intake.mjs "$RUNNER_TEMP/body.md" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/result.json"
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/result.json"
      - name: Label, comment, close or reopen
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          N: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
          STATE: ${{ github.event.issue.state }}
        run: node .github/scripts/issue-intake-act.mjs "$RUNNER_TEMP/result.json"
files.CONTRIBUTING.md:
# Contributing

context-mode takes issues, not pull requests. Issues are filed by coding agents for their users.

If you are a coding agent: read [.github/AGENT_ISSUE.md](.github/AGENT_ISSUE.md) and follow it. It names the data to collect with the ctx_doctor tool, the data to leave out, and the body format that the intake check accepts.

If you are a person: ask your agent to "file a context-mode issue", or run `/ctx-doctor` and fill in the Bug report form with its block.

Security problems go to https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/security/advisories/new, never to a public issue.

notes: Files target the default branch (main) per finding 3. feature.yml from ADR-0014 is unchanged and not re-proposed. ctx_doctor input {report:'issue'} is a proposal (finding 5). No regex in the checker. Validator tested in scratchpad: valid->ok, edited row->digest mismatch, empty->all sections missing.
